title: Knight VS 2 Rooks
reviewNotes: Two branches from stable seven-piece position after Qa1+ ...Rd1 at 27 seconds. Saved boards resolve captioned Qc4 to Qc3+, then ...Rdd2 Qc1+ ...Rd1 Qe3+. Both blockers on e2 reach actual Nf3 mate, with Qxe2+ sacrificing the queen against ...Ne2+. Source resets are not treated as consecutive moves.
transcript: White's brilliant idea is queen to A4 check, now forcing the king to move. Of course, if the king comes out, this would be a checkmate. And if the rook covers, we're going to just take it and then take this knight. But black can of course play king to E1 and now prepare to build a shelter with these rooks and knight, and it is going to be impossible for white to break through. But white has a brilliant plan in mind and plays queen to A1 check. The only move that covers is rook to D1. But now white follows up with queen to C4 and after the rook comes back up, it almost seems like white is trying to repeat moves and go for a draw by repetition, but that is not the case. White follows up with queen to E3 check. And now if the rook was to cover, knight to F3 would be a checkmate. But of course, black can cover with a knight and deliver a check at the same time. And here it seems like black has created the perfect setup to protect the black king. And now white will have to move the king and have no win. But whenever you have an idea in mind, you have to ask yourself, what if I do it anyway? And in this case, the winning idea is to sacrifice the queen. Queen takes E2 check. Forces rook takes E2. And now we have the rooks in the perfect position to still deliver knight to F3 checkmate.
